title: Disjoint Sets for 846- and 847-Round Trivium Superpolies
summary: A search found no disjoint set for the 846- and 847-round Trivium superpolies; whether one enabling reduction to linear systems exists remains open.

formal_statement.body: The superpolies of 846-- and 847-round Trivium are neither linear nor quadratic and involve all secret variables. The disjoint-set technique can reduce solving a system of nonlinear or non-quadratic equations to solving multiple systems of linear equations, but a search found no disjoint set for these superpolies. Determine whether a disjoint set enabling this reduction exists for the 846-- and 847-round Trivium superpolies, and construct one if it does.

scope.domain: Cube-attack cryptanalysis of the nonlinear, nonquadratic 846- and 847-round Trivium superpolies involving all secret variables.
parameters: 846 and 847 rounds — the Trivium round counts defining the target superpolies
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether a disjoint set enabling reduction to multiple linear systems exists for these Trivium superpolies, and construct one if it does.

citations.label: Stretching Cube Attacks: Improved Methods to Recover Massive Superpolies

progress.summary: The source reports that its search for a disjoint set for the 846- and 847-round Trivium superpolies found none. It provides neither a construction nor a nonexistence proof.
